items.evidence: Give-all test on Hookshot, 2026-11-17: written live through the store (both copies); written and read back; individually checked in game 2026-11-17 (user): shown in the inventory screen but the ability was not granted. [2026-11-18] STRENGTH MECHANISM CONFIRMED: the separate record is the unnamed live Enum 0x59979321 (values None/Low/Middle/High, from the GameDataList). Getting Goron's Bracelet normally set None→Low. Setting it to None live made bombs unholdable (pulled out, then put away) and bomb flowers unliftable, even with the bracelet owned. Setting it back to Low restored both. So holding a bomb needs strength ≥ Low. The also[] write grants the enum. Grant via trainer pending the build.

Keys verified by hash in slot_05/progress.sav: IsGet.Armor_Child_Mask_Amiibo0 (Bool), PouchData.Armor_Child_Mask_Amiibo0.StockNum (Int - the leaf record; the bare PouchData.Armor_Child_Mask_Amiibo0 is only a key prefix) and HavePlayedGetEvent.Armor_Child_Mask_Amiibo0 (Bool); the pickup event is written in also[]. Relabelled from the user's in-game description; not mapped to an unconfirmed amiibo name.

items.label: Young Zelda Mask (amiibo B)
items.evidence: In game (0.3.1, Hookshot, child era, 2026-11-18, user): the grant gave her the mask - obtainable via grant confirmed. Per the user (from online sources) this is the Young Zelda mask, wearable as a child; relabelled from that identification (not mapped to an amiibo figure name). First-grant quirk (unexplained): in the same session, granted right after slot A (Fairy Kid) with identical live values (IsGet/StockNum/HavePlayedGetEvent all true) it did NOT appear; it appeared after reloading a save / granting on a file that did not already have the other amiibo mask. Untested idea (note, not a finding): the mask menu may only refresh on load. Keys verified by hash in slot_05/progress.sav: IsGet.Armor_Child_Mask_Amiibo1 (Bool), PouchData.Armor_Child_Mask_Amiibo1.StockNum (Int - leaf record) and HavePlayedGetEvent.Armor_Child_Mask_Amiibo1 (Bool); the pickup event is written in also[]. Row kept and confirmed.

items.label: Bunny Hood
items.evidence: Give-all test on Hookshot, 2026-11-17: written live through the store (both copies) and read back. Individually checked in game 2026-11-17 (user): granting fills the inventory screen but does not equip to the D-pad - the previously equipped mask stays until equipped manually. The equipped-mask state is a separate record (RE pending, P5 equipment objects). [2026-11-17] The grant also writes the pickup event listed in also[] — the event that grants the item's in-game effect, not just the inventory flag. Added after in-game testing showed the item flag alone leaves it in the inventory without its effect. Event key confirmed in the save catalog and the Cross-Platform Cheat Tools crossref. [pending: in-game]

In game (2026-11-17): the songbook flag is IsGet.Item_Melody_ScarecrowSong (0x5E86FB4D) — setting it put the song in the songbook immediately, and every other learned song in the save has IsGet.Item_Melody_<song> = true; AskBonooru_listentothesong is only a Bonooru conversation step (with it on, saved, plus the notes, the song was NOT in the songbook). So the flag field (currently AskBonooru) is the wrong key — left as-is while the Scarecrow fix is on hold. The save-file note write is likely [pending: in-game]: a notes + timing-blob write loads cleanly in game (only 2 of 11,925 keys changed); the blob is a resize write (+376 bytes) the trainer's same-size-only writer doesn't do yet, so the trainer writes the notes only. Full grant unconfirmed: playing the song as a child (IsGet on) froze the game (process exited, nothing saved) — cause unknown (progress values like Step_SubEvent_GetScarecrow not advanced, or the child path is unhandled — in the original only adults use it); adult play untested.
